slides.title: Long context is not memory
slides.caption: Most leading models read a million tokens in one call. That invites skipping the memory. Models get worse at finding things long before the window is full.

slides.title: What we will cover
slides.caption: The one-million-token window is standard. Two pricing regimes. Effective context is a fraction of nominal. Long context against retrieval. What ten million tokens costs.

slides.title: The window is standard
slides.caption: As of September 2026, nine model families offer a million tokens or more. One claims ten million. The claim and the useful length are different numbers.

slides.title: Two pricing regimes
slides.caption: Some vendors bill flat across the window. Others bill the whole request at double once it passes a threshold. Memory workloads sit on the wrong side of the threshold.

slides.title: Effective context is a fraction
slides.caption: One test removes word overlap between question and evidence. On it, effective context is 1K to 16K for models that claim 1M to 10M.

slides.title: Four more lines of evidence
slides.caption: Almost all models drop sharply past the plain needle test. Synthetic tests do not predict real tasks. Every model degrades with length. The vendors say so themselves.

slides.title: The 2026 follow-ups reach a million
slides.caption: The leader at 128 thousand tokens is not the leader at one million. Frontier models miss dangerous actions far more often after 800 thousand tokens.

slides.title: Long context against retrieval
slides.caption: Within the window, long context wins on accuracy by 7 to 13 points. It loses on cost by ten to twenty-six times. Past the window, plain retrieval collapses too.

slides.title: Past the window, both collapse
slides.caption: A 2026 benchmark tests question answering over 128 thousand to ten million tokens. At four million, plain retrieval scores 2.4 and a memory agent 22.1. At ten million, 1.2 and 11.1.

slides.title: What ten million tokens costs
slides.caption: At list price, one ten-million-token prompt costs between one dollar and six hundred dollars. No one-million-token model accepts it in a single call.

slides.title: Caching helps a static corpus
slides.caption: A cached read of ten million tokens costs three cents to twenty dollars. It helps only when the same tokens are asked again within the cache lifetime.

slides.title: What to remember
slides.caption: A window bounds one call and proves nothing about what will be found. Effective context is thousands of tokens, not millions. Cost tiers start where memory workloads begin.
